headline_claim: Eating Chocolate Every Day Is Good for Your Heart
primary_claim: In an observational cohort followed for 11 years, adults who reported eating more chocolate had a modestly lower rate of cardiovascular events than those who ate little or none.
epistemic_gaps: This is an observational cohort, so it can only show an association — it cannot establish that chocolate itself lowers cardiovascular risk.
Reverse causation is unaddressed: healthier people (or those without early heart symptoms) may simply feel freer to eat more chocolate.
Residual confounding is likely — regular chocolate eaters may differ systematically in income, overall diet, and activity, none of which are fully controlled.
Chocolate intake was self-reported via food-frequency questionnaire, which is imprecise and prone to recall bias.
A portion of cocoa and chocolate research is industry-funded, which does not invalidate the finding but warrants caution on framing.
